# Review open-source licenses and software dependencies

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before distributing software, changing deployment models or accepting dependencies with unresolved licensing. A reviewed dependency and license inventory with approved notices, obligations and exception decisions.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Inventory direct, transitive and bundled components

agent-runnable


Generate a component inventory for the actual build, including copied code, containers, assets and model or dataset components. Record versions, origin and the exact license text where available.

- Sources: [GitHub Open Source Guides: the legal side](https://opensource.guide/legal/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Describe how the components are used

agent-runnable


Distinguish internal use, hosted service, distribution, modifications and linking or packaging choices. Record missing or conflicting licenses and the build paths that include each component.

- Sources: [GitHub Open Source Guides: the legal side](https://opensource.guide/legal/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Review obligations and compatibility

human · human approval required


Qualified counsel or the licensing reviewer evaluates the actual licenses and use model. Approve, replace or isolate components with unresolved rights rather than assuming a public repository grants reuse permission.

- Sources: [GitHub Open Source Guides: the legal side](https://opensource.guide/legal/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Prepare notices and the compliance package

agent-runnable


Assemble the approved attribution, license notices and any source or offer materials the reviewer requires. Ensure the package matches the released artifacts and keep customer-specific contractual promises separate.

- Sources: [GitHub Open Source Guides: the legal side](https://opensource.guide/legal/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Approve release and maintain the inventory

human · human approval required


The authorized reviewer confirms unresolved blockers are closed or explicitly accepted before release. Integrate dependency changes into review and retain the evidence used for the approved version.

- Verify: A reviewed dependency and license inventory with approved notices, obligations and exception decisions.
- Sources: [GitHub Open Source Guides: the legal side](https://opensource.guide/legal/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)
